papers.title: Machine Learning methods for interatomic potentials: application to boron carbide
papers.abstract: Total energies of crystal structures can be calculated to high precision using quantum-based density functional theory (DFT) methods, but the calculations can be time consuming and scale badly with system size. Cluster expansions of total energy as a linear superposition of pair, triplet and higher interactions can efficiently approximate the total energies but are best suited to simple lattice structures. To model the total energy of boron carbide, with a complex crystal structure, we explore the utility of machine learning methods ($L_1$-penalized regression, neural network, Gaussian process and support vector regression) that capture certain non-linear effects associated with many-body interactions despite requiring only pair frequencies as input. Our interaction models are combined with Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate the thermodynamics of chemical ordering.

summary_en.motivation: To efficiently approximate density functional theory total energies for complex crystal structures like boron carbide.
summary_en.method: Machine learning methods (L1-penalized regression, neural network, Gaussian process, support vector regression) are trained on pair frequencies to capture many-body interactions.
summary_en.result: The surrogate models are combined with Monte Carlo simulations to study the thermodynamics of chemical ordering.
summary_en.validation: Accuracy is validated against DFT reference calculations.
